text.en: Meena shouted in an empty hall and heard her voice come back. "Sound reflects," said her teacher.

Sound waves are longitudinal waves. Wave velocity is the distance the wave travels in unit time, and V = n x wavelength, where n is the frequency. Sound travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids and slowest in gases, because gases are the least elastic.
Sound reflects from a surface following the laws of reflection: the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. An echo is heard when the reflected sound reaches the ear at least 0.1 second after the original, so the reflecting surface must be at least about 17 m away. Echoes are used to measure the depth of the sea and the speed of sound. The ear trumpet, megaphone and sound board use reflection.
The Doppler effect is the apparent change in the frequency of sound due to relative motion between the source and the listener. The pitch rises as the source approaches and falls as it moves away. It is used in radar, medical scans and speed guns.

problem.en: A sound of frequency 500 Hz has wavelength 0.68 m. Find its speed.

prompt.en: A friend says The Doppler effect changes the speed of sound. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: It changes the apparent frequency, not the speed.

points.en: Echo needs at least 0.1 s gap.
